extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating submissions to the CVPR 2024 conference, covering core evaluation principles, review quality, ethics/conflicts, and special-policy areas (arXiv, datasets, LLMs, supplementary material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether papers are "technically sound and make a contribution to the field."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Look for what is good or stimulating in the paper, and what knowledge advancement it has made."

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty versus performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not conflate novelty and performance: lack of state-of-the-art accuracy is not by itself a reason to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The fact that a proposed method does not exceed the state-of-the-art accuracy on an existing benchmark dataset is not grounds for rejection by itself." Novel conceptual or methodological contribution can merit acceptance even without beating benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive and detailed reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be substantive and detailed rather than terse or checklist-style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discouraged: "Bullet lists with one short sentence per bullet." Emphasized: provide thorough discussion to justify recommendations and help authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis for your recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity for novelty claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific about novelty claims and back assertions with concrete references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide "specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related" when claiming novelty or differentiating from prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize discussion over score
rubrics_metrics.description: The written discussion is more important than the numeric score for communicating evaluation rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Your discussion, more than your score, will help the authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis for your recommendation." Focus on clear justification rather than relying on the score alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not actively identify authors or share submissions; keep papers confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "You should not show the paper to anyone else" except designated helpers. Never reveal author identities and avoid actions that would break the double-blind process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reviewing papers where a conflict of interest exists (shared institution, recent collaboration, advisor/advisee relationship, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict arises, contact the Area Chair immediately. Do not accept or complete reviews when conflicts apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional tone and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Write a courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful review that you would be proud to sign with your name." Avoid personal attacks, salty language, or unprofessional commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of arXiv/preprint work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not demand comparisons to recent preprints or reject solely because prior work appears on arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers "shouldn't demand comparisons to recent preprints or reject solely based on prior arXiv work." However, authors should acknowledge papers that "directly and obviously inspired them." Use judgment when assessing relevance of very recent preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers using withdrawn datasets require very close scrutiny but are not automatically grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: using a withdrawn dataset like DukeMTMC-ReID warrants careful examination of ethical/data provenance issues; evaluate thoroughly rather than reject outright on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed and disallowed use of LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Language models may be used to polish wording, but reviewers must not expose submissions to LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers "may use language models to polish wording but must never show submissions to LLMs—doing so constitutes confidentiality violation." Treat any external tooling that accesses manuscript text as a potential breach unless explicitly allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material should only be consulted when necessary and must not contain substantially improved results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only look at supplementary material if needed to evaluate claims; ensure that core claims and principal results are present in the main submission and that supplemental files do not hide materially better results.
